title: fix(rest,runtime)!: a /data PATCH or DELETE refuses a version token that can never carry a version, on both doors
body:
Fixes #23492
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

Both doors of `PATCH /data/:object/:id` and `DELETE /data/:object/:id` now judge every optimistic-concurrency token a caller sends, or refuse it `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` before the protocol is asked. The two doors are `RestServer` (`packages/rest`) and the runtime dispatcher's `/data` domain (`packages/runtime`), the only door on a `createHonoApp` host. A token that can never carry a version is no longer read as "no token", so it can no longer hide a stale `If-Match`. One rule lands in both doors together, and they stay the statement-for-statement mirrors that PR #23460 and PR #23490 made them.

Dispatched by the `domain:cli` seat 2 PM (claim `6171438684`, branch `claude/issue-23492-empty-version-token`), session `session_01Q9PZ5Pzqcus4woVvTZwWNU`.

## What was wrong (measured)

Both doors read `bodyVersion ?? If-Match` on `PATCH` (`?expectedVersion ?? If-Match` on `DELETE`), and forwarded the token only when it was truthy. Measured on the rig these pins extend, on `origin/main` `3a2adc8835`: a real better-sqlite3 store, the real ObjectQL and protocol, `RestServer`'s registered handler and the real `dispatch()` side by side, with the row read back after every request. The two doors answered identically in every row.

| request | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `PATCH`, body `expectedVersion: ''`, stale `If-Match` | `200`, row written | `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, row unchanged |
| `PATCH`, body `''`, no `If-Match` | `200`, written | `400` |
| `PATCH`, body `false`, stale `If-Match` | `200`, written | `400` |
| `PATCH`, body `false`, no `If-Match` | `200`, written | `400` |
| `PATCH`, body `'   '` (blank), stale `If-Match` | `200`, written (forwarded; the protocol reads blank as no token) | `400` |
| `PATCH`, body `[]`, stale `If-Match` | `200`, written (see note 1) | `400` |
| `PATCH`, body `true` | `409`, judged as `'true'` | `400` |
| `PATCH`, body `{}` | `409`, judged as `'[object Object]'` | `400` |
| `PATCH`, body `0`, with or without a stale `If-Match` | `200`, written (dropped) | `409`, judged as `'0'` |
| `PATCH`, empty `If-Match`, no body token | `200`, written | `400` |
| `DELETE`, `?expectedVersion=`, stale `If-Match` | `200`, row deleted | `400`, row kept |
| `DELETE`, `?expectedVersion=`, no `If-Match` | `200`, deleted | `400` |
| `DELETE`, `?expectedVersion=` blank, stale `If-Match` | `200`, deleted | `400` |
| `DELETE`, empty `If-Match`, no query token | `200`, deleted | `400` |
| unchanged: body `null`, stale `If-Match` | `409` | `409` |
| unchanged: body `5`; `?expectedVersion=0` | `409` | `409` |
| unchanged: `""` (body, query or header) | the protocol's `400` | the protocol's `400` |

Note 1: the `[]` row's "before" was read with this PR's refusal ablated. That leaves the forward test `!= null`, which forwards `[]` exactly as the truthiness test did. `String([])` is `''`, which the protocol reads as no token.

## The rule

There is one function per door, identical in both: `versionTokenRefusal(token, spelling)`, in `rest-server.ts` and in `domains/data.ts`. It sorts a token three ways:

- **Absent:** `undefined` or `null`. The body key or query name falls through to `If-Match`, and no `If-Match` either is the legal unguarded write. This is unchanged.
- **Judged:** a string with something in it, or a finite number. The door forwards `String(token)`, and the forward test is now `!= null`, not truthiness.
- **Refused `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`:** anything else: an empty or blank string, a boolean, an array, an object.

The body key is still stripped from the patch whatever its value. PR #23490's pin (no `expectedVersion` ever reaches the engine as a field) still holds.

## Rulings applied, and the judgments this PR made

- **Ruled, not reopened:** #13576's maintainer decision #20 ①, recorded at `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` (`MalformedVersionTokenError`). A token shape that can never carry a version is refused `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, neither read as "no token" nor answered `409`. This PR applies that rule to the body and query spellings. "Fall through to `If-Match`" was not offered.
- **The empty `If-Match` (PM hypothesis (d)) is in scope, on both doors.** Why:
  - An empty `If-Match` is not the absent header that the ruling keeps as an unguarded write. The caller asked for a guard and sent nothing to judge, the same shape as body `expectedVersion: ''` with no header, which the ruling refuses.
  - RFC 7232 does not admit an empty `If-Match` value at all, unlike `""`, which the platform already refuses.
  - No first-party producer sends one. `@objectstack/client`'s `data.update` and `data.delete`, and objectui's `ApiDataSource` and `MetadataClient`, all omit the header for a falsy `ifMatch` (grep: `if (opts?.ifMatch)` / `opts.ifMatch ? … : …`).
  - Leaving it out would need a second rule ("an empty header is absent") beside the one this PR adds.
- **`true`, arrays and objects are refused too.** `false` refused while `true` is answered `409` would be two answers for one type. `[]` stringifies to `''` and wrote unguarded, the defect itself, one spelling over.
- **Blank strings are refused.** The protocol reads a blank token as no token (its docblock, "per the ruling's clause ②"), so a blank body token beside a stale `If-Match` wrote unguarded. That is the same defect.
- **`0` is judged as `'0'`, not refused.** It is a number, and every other number was already judged. This leaves the declared `z.string()` unwidened and unenforced on numbers, which is not this card (see Acceptance notes).

## How each door renders the refusal

Both doors build the refusal with the one constructor, `validationFailure(sentence, [])` from `@objectstack/types`, and render it with their own classifier. The two doors answer the same status, `code` and sentence; a parity pin holds them to it.

- **`RestServer` THROWS it into the route's own catch.** `mapDataError` renders it as `{ error, code: 'VALIDATION_FAILED', fields: [], object }`, the envelope that door already gives the protocol's `""` refusal. A hand-built `res.status(400).json(...)` body was the first draft. `check:route-envelope` refused it (`siblingCode: found 41, declared 39 — a NEW non-conforming body`), so no body is hand-built here.
- **The dispatcher RETURNS `deps.errorFromThrown(...)`.** The body is `{ success: false, error: { code: 'VALIDATION_FAILED', message, httpStatus: 400, details: { fields: [] } } }`.
- **On a `createHonoApp` host:** measured through the real `createHonoApp` over the rebuilt runtime `dist`, with a recording protocol, in the same set-up as `packages/qa/http-conformance`'s `hono-*.conformance.test.ts`. That measurement was a scratch test, not committed.
  - All five refusal shapes (`PATCH` body `''` with a stale `If-Match`, body `false`, an empty `If-Match`, `DELETE ?expectedVersion=` with a stale `If-Match`, an empty `If-Match` on `DELETE`) answered `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` on the wire, with the protocol never called.
  - The refusals the protocol THROWS out of `dispatch()` still render as `500` there (the record is unchanged): `409 CONCURRENT_UPDATE`, and the `400` for `""` (measured: a thrown `{ code: 'VALIDATION_FAILED', status: 400 }` answered `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`). The catch-all reads only an error's `statusCode`. Rendering their declared status is a separate change; #23365 remains open for it.

## Tests

Pins extend PR #23490's and PR #23460's rig: `packages/runtime/src/domains/data-update-expected-version.test.ts` and `data-delete-expected-version.test.ts`.

- **Per door, `PATCH`:** `''` and `false` each beside a stale `If-Match` and beside no header, blank beside a stale `If-Match`, `true`, `[]` beside a stale `If-Match`, and an empty `If-Match` alone. Each asserts `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`, `updateData` never asked, and the row unchanged.
- **Per door, `DELETE`:** `?expectedVersion=` beside a stale `If-Match` and beside no header, a blank `?expectedVersion`, and an empty `If-Match` alone. Each asserts `400`, `deleteData` never asked, and the row kept.
- **Per door, protocol parity:** the door's refusal has the same status and `code` as the protocol's own refusal of `""`. That token is shown to reach the protocol.
- **Per door, controls:** a `null` body token is no token (a stale `If-Match` beside it is `409`). Body `0` is judged as `'0'` (`409`), beside an `If-Match` naming the current version.
- **Cross-door:** each refused shape gets the same status, `code` and sentence on both doors.

Results:

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/domains/data-update-expected-version.test.ts src/domains/data-delete-expected-version.test.ts`: `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 84 passed (84)`, at `6d399e780b`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest run test`: `Test Files 283 passed (283)`, `Tests 5852 passed | 326 skipped (6178)`, at `6d399e780b`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime run test`: `Test Files 380 passed (380)`, `Tests 5617 passed | 19 skipped (5636)`, at `b763612ee8`. The one commit after it changes only how `RestServer` renders the refusal, and the two pin files above were re-run on it.
- `typecheck` for `@objectstack/rest` and `@objectstack/runtime` passed at `6d399e780b`: `tsc --noEmit`, then `check:test-typecheck` OK on both.

### Ablations

Each ablation goes through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, with a restore trap and a restore proven by blob equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`. Both doors' code under test resolves to source (`@objectstack/rest` is aliased to `src` in runtime's vitest config, and the dispatcher is a relative import), so no `dist` leg applies.

| mutation | anchor on disk (before / during / after) | result |
|---|---|---|
| `RestServer`'s refusal dropped (`versionTokenRefusal` returns `undefined` first), at `6d399e780b` | 1 / 0 / 1 | 27 red, 57 green. Every `RestServer` `[#23492]` refusal row is red (PATCH 9 of 11; the 2 green are the `null` and `0` controls; DELETE 5 of 5), the cross-door rows are red (8 + 4 + 1 `[#23462]` parity row), and every catch-all row stays green (11 + 5). |
| the dispatcher's refusal dropped, at `b763612ee8` (`data.ts` unchanged since) | 1 / 0 / 1 | 27 red, 57 green: the exact mirror. The catch-all rows are red, and every `RestServer` row is green. |
| `RestServer`'s forward back to truthy (3 sites) | 3 / 0 / 3 | 1 red: `RestServer`'s `0` control. |
| the dispatcher's forward back to truthy (2 sites) | 2 / 0 / 2 | 1 red: the catch-all's `0` control. |

## Gates

These were run locally on the final commit `6d399e780b`:

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 65 commands, and all 65 exited `0`. `--ran` (with exit codes) reports `65 derived, 65 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`.
- The four roster gates whose roster sits in one of this PR's directories also exited `0`: `check-changeset-fixed`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:filter-alias-parity` and `check:route-ledger-census`.
- `pnpm lint` was run as a declared narrowing. The same binary and flags (`eslint --no-inline-config`) ran over the four changed `.ts` files and exited `0`. As a positive control, the same invocation on two of those paths, through `--stdin-filename` with an injected restricted import, exited `1`, so the paths are linted, not ignored. CI runs the whole tree.

## Acceptance notes

None of these is filed by this PR; each finding goes to the seat in the report.

- `UpdateDataRequestSchema.expectedVersion` is declared `z.string()`, yet both doors accept a body number and judge `String(n)`. Measured: body `5` is answered `409` on both doors, not refused as off-spec. Refusing numbers is not this card.
- The protocol's `assertVersionTokenNotMalformed` still reads `''` and blank as no token. So an in-process caller of `updateData` or `deleteData` (not through either door) still writes unguarded with such a token. This is a read-only inference; no other public door was measured.
- The spec's `expectedVersion` describe names only `""` as refused. It does not say that an empty or blank token is refused at the doors. The text is not contradicted, but it is narrower than the behaviour.
- `?expectedVersion` as a query on `PATCH` is still read by neither door; the spec declares only the body field or `If-Match` there. This is unchanged and has no carrier.
- The `createHonoApp` `500` for protocol-thrown refusals is #23365's.
